correctness.rationale: An independent rank argument verifies the joint law. In decreasing score order consider only the cells incident with the selected k rows or selected k columns of a specified matching M. There are k(r+c−k) such cells, with uniform relative rank. The first must be in M: otherwise it blocks one of the desired cells. Conditional on which selected cell is first, that cell is already a mutual maximum and the relative order of all other entries in the union stays uniform. The new constrained union for the remaining matching is contained in that remainder; it excludes the first cell but retains relevant cross-cells. Induction gives probability 1/(r+c−k) times the (k−1)-cell inclusion probability, yielding 1/(r+c−1) falling k. Multiplying by (r falling k)(c falling k) gives the factorial moments of Hypergeom(r+c−1,r,c); finite support determines the PMF. The global maximum guarantees K≥1. Permuting rows and columns acts transitively on matchings of fixed size; dividing the PMF by their number gives exactly 1/[c(k−1)! binom(r+c−1,c)] per labelled full set. The hypergeometric variance is as stated, with the separate singleton case; one-row or one-column boards have K=1. This checks frozen RESULT.md lines 5–30 and 38–83. VERIFICATION.md and verify_rook_maxima.py were inspected, not executed.

Sorting the selected scores and integrating powers yields k!/∏_{j=1}^k j(r+c−j), so the displayed joint probabilities follow directly. In the bipartite nearest-neighbor graph with shared iid edge weights, orient a choice at each vertex toward its unique minimum-weight edge. Every directed cycle must have length two, since successive distinct edge weights along a longer cycle would have to strictly decrease. Each weak component contains a unique directed cycle, making its component count exactly the reciprocal-minimum count.
